$comment: Generated by scripts/gen-api.sh - do not edit. Every token, type and service a plugin may use. Regenerate after changing core/, services/ or modules/common/widgets/; scripts/check-qml.sh fails if this is stale.
readMeFirst: Colours: use Theme.*, never Appearance.* - Theme is the stable API and names surfaces by role.
A desktop widget draws on a wallpaper: give it an opaque backing (Theme.solid) or it is invisible.
Read settings as settings.<key> (declared in the manifest) - the object has one typed property per key, so binding to a key is a precise dependency.
Never shell out for clipboard, notifications, HTTP or opening a URL: PluginUtils does all four without a subprocess.
Commands are lists, never strings: PluginUtils.exec(["cmd", arg]).
Annotate function parameter and return types, void included, or Quickshell will not expose the function over IPC.
No `required property` in a file loaded by URL - it cannot be constructed and the Loader silently draws nothing.

materialSymbol.description: A Material Symbols Rounded ligature name, e.g. battery_full. Not a file path.

qmlFile.description: Path to a .qml file, relative to the plugin folder.

barWidget.description: A widget the user can place in the bar. Its root should be a PluginBarWidget.

id.description: Also the layout token stored in the user's bar config. Reusing a built-in id replaces that built-in.

materialPill.description: Whether the bar paints its pill behind this widget.

multipleAllowed.description: May appear more than once in a layout.

zone.description: Where to place the widget the first time the plugin is enabled. Without this, enabling the plugin appears to do nothing until the user drags the widget in from Settings -> Bar. Applied once and recorded; removing it afterwards is respected.

zoneOrder.description: Order relative to other auto-placed widgets in the same zone.

desktopWidget.description: A draggable widget on the desktop. Its root should be a PluginDesktopCard (header, content, footer, resize, persistence) or a bare PluginBackgroundWidget.

id.description: Must match the widgetId the QML sets, or position and size are stored under a different key than they are read from.

enabledByDefault.description: Whether the widget is on the desktop as soon as the plugin is enabled.

quickToggle.description: A tile in the sidebar's quick settings. Inherit AndroidQuickToggleButton and it works in the classic panel too.

classicEntry.description: A different file for the classic panel. Omit to use the same one.

menu.description: Expanded panel shown when the tile's chevron is tapped.

settingsPage.description: A whole page in Settings with its own navigation entry. Prefer settingsSections unless the plugin really owns a page's worth of UI.

settingsSection.description: A section injected into an existing Settings page, so a plugin's settings sit next to the related built-in ones and disappear when it is switched off.

page.description: Host page name, matched case-insensitively. Pages that host sections: Interface, Bar, Desktop, Services, Appearance, Advanced.

launcherAction.description: A static entry in the launcher, matched by name. For answering queries dynamically use searchProviders instead.

script.description: A script inside the plugin folder, run instead of exec. Anything typed after the action name is appended as arguments.

searchProvider.description: A live query handler in the launcher: a calculator, a converter, a dictionary, a note search. Its root must be a PluginSearchProvider. Fields here override the QML's own defaults.

prefix.description: Only consulted for queries starting with this. Empty means every query - correct only for a provider that can tell from the query itself whether it applies.

order.description: Lower sorts this provider's block of results earlier.

contextMenuItem.description: A row in the desktop right-click menu. Exactly one of ipc, panel, exec or entry decides what it does.

order.description: Position among all rows. The shell own rows sit at 10 (Wallpaper), 20 (Widgets) and 100 (Settings).

entry.description: A submenu the plugin draws itself, opened on hover.

badge.description: A PluginBus topic whose retained value is shown at the right of the row, e.g. "dropover:count". Updates live while the menu is open.

osdIndicator.description: A HUD shown over everything and dismissed on a timer: a countdown, a progress bar, a status flash. Show it with OsdRegistry.show("id"). The QML draws content only; the shell owns the window, placement and timeout.

timeout.description: Milliseconds. 0 uses the user's configured OSD timeout.

shortcut.description: A keybind, registered as the compositor global quickshell:<id>. The shell never edits the compositor config - `qs -c end4-pC ipc call plugins shortcuts` prints the exact line to paste.

suggestedKey.description: Compositor syntax, e.g. "SUPER SHIFT, B". A suggestion printed to the user, not something the shell binds.

ipcCall.description: Calls a function on a PluginIpc, in-process. Cheaper and more capable than spawning a command.

target.description: The PluginIpc's target, which defaults to the plugin id.

args.description: Arguments, with the substitutions $menuX, $menuY and $screen available in a context menu row.

argv.description: A command as a list, never a shell string: ["notify-send", "hi"]. Each element is one argument, so nothing in it is ever interpreted by a shell.

appearanceColor.description: A colour role name understood by Appearance.getColorFromName.

key.description: Becomes a QML property, so it must be a valid identifier and cannot be a QML reserved word (data, children, parent, objectName, state, visible, enabled...). PluginConfig refuses and warns about the ones that would not work.

label.description: Shown next to the control. Defaults to the key.

placeholder.description: Greyed hint inside an empty text field. string type only.

group.description: Settings sharing a group are rendered as one titled block, in the order the groups first appear. Ungrouped settings come first.

default.description: Required in practice: a setting with no default reads as an empty value of its type.

options.description: enum only. Either plain strings, or { value, label } for a nicer control.

panelAction.description: Opens a panel by id. Arguments may use the substitutions $menuX, $menuY and $screen, which resolve to where the menu was opened.

id.description: Panel id, as declared by a manifest panels entry or by PanelRegistry built-ins.

args.description: Passed to PanelRegistry.open and readable as PanelRegistry.state(id).args.

theme.summary: Semantic tokens over the Material You palette. Import qs.core and use Theme.<token>.

members.name: dark
members.doc: True when the generated scheme is dark. Prefer picking colours from here over branching on this, but it is occasionally the only way (picking an asset, say).

members.name: panel
members.doc: Over the wallpaper, or anywhere with no shell panel behind it, use `solid`.

members.name: surface
members.doc: Kept as aliases because "surface" is what everyone reaches for first.

members.name: solid
members.doc: Fully opaque, for a desktop widget or anything drawn straight onto the wallpaper, where a translucent layer has nothing to composite against.

members.doc: A hairline. Already low-contrast; do not also fade it.

members.doc: For anything that has to sit over the wallpaper, or over a scrim.

members.name: textFaint
members.doc: Tertiary text: hints, placeholders, disabled labels.

members.name: textOnPanel
members.doc: Text directly on a panel background rather than on a block inside it.

members.name: accent
members.doc: `accent` is the wallpaper's colour, and is what a plugin should reach for to look like it belongs. `onAccent` is the only readable text colour on top of it.

members.name: accentBlock
members.doc: A filled accent block big enough to hold text - a card, a selected row.

members.name: accentMuted
members.doc: The quieter accent, for chips and toggles that should not shout.

members.name: error
members.doc: Material has no warning or success role, so these are the closest honest mappings rather than invented colours: they stay inside the generated scheme and therefore still look delib

members.name: notice
members.doc: Distinct from accent and from error, which is all "warning" and "success" really need from a generated palette.

members.name: state
members.doc: Material draws interaction as a translucent layer over the base colour rather than as a different colour, which is why these are opacities and not colours. `StateLayer` applies the

members.name: pad
members.doc: Spacing and padding. `m` is the default gap between related things.

members.name: radius
members.doc: Corner radii. `m` is a card; `full` is a pill.

members.name: anim
members.doc: Components, for `Behavior on x { animation: Theme.anim.fast.number... }`. Using these rather than a hand-written NumberAnimation is what makes a plugin move like the rest of the sh

members.name: motion
members.doc: Enter is slower than exit on purpose (400 against 200): something arriving has to be understood, something leaving only has to get out of the way.

members.name: fade
members.doc: ---------------------------------------------------------------- utilities Same colour, more transparent. `amount` 0..1, where 1 is invisible.

members.name: mix
members.args: a: color, b: color, amount: real
members.doc: Blend two colours. `amount` is how much of `b`.

members.name: on
members.doc: A readable text colour for an arbitrary background - a wallpaper sample, a user-chosen colour, an album cover. `m3surface` and `m3onSurface` are always one light and one dark, swap

members.name: harmonize
members.doc: Pull an arbitrary colour towards the wallpaper's palette, so third-party assets and hard-coded brand colours stop looking pasted on.

members.name: role
members.doc: Anything from `Appearance` by role name, for the rare case this shortlist does not cover: Theme.role("colTertiaryHover"). Returns transparent if unknown, so a typo is a visible mis

members.name: createPaletteFromColor
members.doc: Generating one is about ten milliseconds of arithmetic - six tonal palettes, twenty-seven gamut-mapped tones each. Fine on a track change, wrong per frame: cache it in a property.

members.name: createTonalPalette
members.doc: Just the ramp: { hue, chroma, tones: { 0..100 }, tone(n) }. For a widget that wants five shades of one colour rather than a whole scheme.

members.name: toneOf
members.doc: Perceptual lightness, 0..100 - the same axis the tones above are indexed by, so `Theme.toneOf(c) > 60` is a meaningful "is this a light colour".

members.name: mostReadable
members.doc: The more readable of two colours on `background`, by WCAG contrast ratio.
